summary.tagline: The rugged granite peaks and dramatic ridgelines of Scotland's geological jewel.
summary.seo_title: Visiting North Arran | Isle of Arran Travel Guide

travel.headline: Advance Ferry Reservations for the Isle of Arran
travel.reservation: Ferry tickets for vehicles should be booked in advance at all times of the year as services between the mainland and Brodick or Lochranza can be very busy. While entry to the northern mountains is generally open, ferry capacity remains the primary bottleneck for travelers. Check the official carrier for current sailing schedules and status.

days.title: Northern Peaks and Ridges

stops.name: Goatfell
stops.detail: Hike the highest peak on the island for views across the Firth of Clyde or explore the challenging rugged ridge routes connecting Cìr Mhòr and Beinn Tarsuinn.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for island transit; conditions vary based on ferry timing and local roads.
days.note: Mountain weather is highly variable; allow extra time for the steep ascent of the northern granite peaks.

intel.title: Ferry Connections
intel.text: Access the island via ferry from Ardrossan or Troon to Brodick, or via the secondary route from Claonaig to Lochranza. These routes accommodate vehicles but require prior planning during peak periods.

intel.title: Seasonal Demand
intel.text: Ferry services are reported to be very busy year-round. It is recommended to secure transit well before arrival to ensure vehicle space.

intel.title: Trailhead Parking
intel.text: Official evidence does not specify parking capacity at the Goatfell trailheads. Visitors should verify local parking availability in Brodick or near the northern mountain access points upon arrival.

intel.title: Mountain Connectivity
intel.text: Mobile signal strength is not documented for the rugged ridge routes of the northern mountains. Travelers should not rely on digital connectivity for navigation in the high peaks.

intel.title: Island Supplies
intel.text: Fuel and supply availability is not detailed in the provided source evidence. Visitors should check for services in the gateway towns of Brodick or Lochranza before heading into the mountains.

plan.arrival: Arrive via ferry at Brodick or Lochranza; pick up supplies in the village before driving toward the northern mountain trailheads.
plan.vehicle: Cars can be brought on all ferry routes; check rental agreements for island travel and ferry boarding restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Goatfell summit at sunset offers views across the ridges, though hikers must allow time for a safe descent before dark.
